approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

referral_steps.text: Place of Entertainment Permit application: this application is sent to the Police Department for review (Police Code § 1060.2(b)(1); § 1060.5(a)).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Amados at 998 Valencia (31 m away, across the street) holds an active Place of Entertainment permit, showing that live entertainment venues operate successfully on this block of Valencia in NCT-VALENCIA.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Entertainment permit (POE) approved for a restaurant with live music directly across the street confirms that the Entertainment Commission and Planning permit live entertainment on this block. The concept's live shows closing at 1 a.m. with amplified sound will require a POE permit, not Limited Live Performance, consistent with Amados' classification.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral for Amados' Place of Entertainment permit at 998 Valencia (52 m away) in 2014, approved as accessory to retail use in NCT-VALENCIA under § 703.2(b)(1)(C)(viii), showing Planning's treatment of POE applications in the immediate corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral shows Planning approved a POE permit as accessory entertainment, limited to one-third of the retail floor area. For a bar where live entertainment is a primary use (not accessory), the POE application will be scrutinized more closely, and the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy conditions will apply.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral for Type 41 license continuation at 1007 Valencia (45 m away, same block) in January 2008, NCT-VALENCIA, explicitly noting approval does not establish a new bar use, illustrating Planning's distinction between Restaurant (Type 41) and Bar uses in the Mission SUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral states 'Approval does not establish a new bar use at subject location,' confirming Planning treats Type 41 licenses as Restaurant use, not Bar use. The concept seeks to change from the current Type 41 restaurant (Sarita's) to a Bar with Type 42 license, which requires a CUA and demonstrates the pathway is change of use, not license continuation.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Planning referral for Arcana at 2512 Mission (150 m away) in November 2020 approved Restaurant and Nighttime Entertainment uses with a Place of Entertainment permit in NCT-MISSION, showing how Planning treats combined food and live entertainment applications in nearby Mission Street NCT districts.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral demonstrates Planning approved a restaurant with nighttime entertainment (POE permit) in the neighboring NCT-MISSION district without conditions extracted. comparable_cases.why_comparable: Denied Planning referral for Limited Live Performance at Lost Weekend Video, 1034 Valencia (94 m away) in April 2015, NCT-VALENCIA, one of only two denials in the candidate set, showing that not all entertainment applications in NCT-VALENCIA are approved.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from SF Planning that a Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD satisfies § 249.60(b)(2)(C) for 995 Valencia St.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a Preliminary Project Assessment or request a zoning interpretation from the Planning Department asking: 'Does a Type 42 on-sale beer-and-wine license transferred from another bar located within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District satisfy Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) for a new Bar use at 995 Valencia St?' State that the concept is a 40-seat bar with limited kitchen, live entertainment closing at 1 a.m., and beer-and-wine service only, and that the space currently holds a Type 41 restaurant license (Sarita's Grill & Beer). Request a list of which Type 42 licenses within the SUD are on premises that Planning would consider 'Bar' uses eligible for transfer under the SUD rules, or confirm that Planning will accept any active Type 42 from a bar in the district.

filing_playbook.action: Engage a California ABC license broker to identify available Type 42 licenses held by bars within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD and initiate negotiations to purchase and transfer one to 995 Valencia St.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Provide the broker with the Mission SUD boundary map (Planning Code § 249.60) and request a list of active Type 42 licenses on premises within the district where the current use is a bar (not a restaurant with a Type 42, which is rare). Confirm with Planning which addresses qualify. Negotiate the purchase price (expect $20,000 to $60,000 for a Type 42, far less than a Type 47) and an escrow contingent on Planning and ABC approval of the CUA and the license transfer. The broker will file the ABC transfer application after the CUA is approved and the building permit is issued.

filing_playbook.action: File a Health Permit to Operate application with SF DPH after the building permit is issued and the DPH plan check is approved.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the online Health Permit application with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN at least one month before the target opening date. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (2026–27). The permit is issued after the final inspection passes, and service to the public cannot begin before issuance.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, California seller's permit, EIN, RBS training for all alcohol servers, food handler cards, and ASCAP/BMI music licenses before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the SF Business Registration online with the Treasurer & Tax Collector ($55 to $700 depending on projected gross receipts, plus $4 state fee) immediately after forming the legal entity. Obtain the EIN from the IRS (free, same-day online), then register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA (free, needed for the ABC application). Enroll all employees who will serve alcohol in the ABC RBS training ($3 registration plus $10 to $25 course fee per person) within 60 days of hire. Enroll all food-handling employees in the California Food Handler Card course ($7 to $15, valid 3 years). Designate at least one certified food safety manager (ServSafe exam, $100 to $250). Sign up for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses (annual fees roughly $300 to $2,500 each, formula-based on occupancy and music use) to cover recorded and live music legally.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost ranges cover the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45 to 120 days, $2,708 to $3,800), Health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000), and Building permit with change of use (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000). The day range is the time to approval, not to a denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (6 to 10 months from filing to final, including pre-application meeting, environmental review, neighborhood notification, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period) followed by the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60 to 150 days after the CUA is final, including escrow, posting, referrals, and undue-concentration review if protested). The POE permit hearing is scheduled in parallel with the CUA and decided within the same cycle. The building permit and health permit are filed after the CUA is approved and run concurrently during construction (3 to 6 months for plan review, build-out, and inspections). Total elapsed time from CUA filing to opening: roughly 12 to 18 months if the CUA and ABC transfer are approved without appeals or protests. Costs include the CUA fee ($3,100 base, higher if construction valuation exceeds thresholds or First Year Free fee waiver does not apply), POE application fee ($2,708 in 2026–27), building permit fees (percentage of construction cost, estimated $800 to $15,000 for a bar tenant improvement), DPH plan check ($828 to $2,207 depending on scope), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), and the ABC Type 42 license purchase price (not a government fee, estimated $20,000 to $60,000 based on market comparables for Type 42 transfers in San Francisco, excluded from the cost range here). Additional costs not in the range: architect and engineer fees for stamped plans, license broker commission (typically 10% to 15% of the license price), construction costs, and pre-opening legal and consultant fees. The cost range shown is government fees only.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA district inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The concept—a bar with beer-and-wine service, limited kitchen, and live entertainment closing at 1 a.m.—constitutes a change of use from the current restaurant (Sarita's Grill & Beer holds an active Type 41 license issued November 2023). A bar is a conditional use in NCT-VALENCIA and triggers the Mission SUD's requirement to transfer a Type 42 license from another bar within the district. The block is heavily saturated: 9 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, 61 within 1,000 ft, and 24 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft. Only three dated use decisions were found in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft—too few to calculate an approval rate—though the immediate site history shows Planning approved multiple alcohol-license transfers for restaurants over two decades.
